body:
`AnalyticEuropeanMargrabeEngine` divides by the standard deviation of the asset ratio, $\sigma^2 = \sigma_1^2 + \sigma_2^2 - 2\rho\sigma_1\sigma_2$, without handling the case where it vanishes:

- with perfect correlation and equal volatilities, rounding can make the variance slightly negative (about -7e-18 for 20% volatilities and a 180-day expiry), so `std::sqrt` returns NaN and the NPV and all Greeks are NaN;
- with zero volatilities, the NPV is finite but both gammas are NaN, since `nd1/(s1*stdDev)` becomes 0/0.

This PR clamps the variance at zero and, when the standard deviation is below `QL_EPSILON`, treats the ratio as deterministic: the option is worth its discounted intrinsic value $D \cdot \max(Q_1F_1 - Q_2F_2, 0)$, with $N(d_{1,2})$ set to 1, 0, or 1/2 at the money (the same convention as `BlackCalculator`) and zero gammas. The non-degenerate path is unchanged.

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| ρ = 1, σ₁ = σ₂ = 20%, 180 days | NPV = NaN | 9.35733 (= $S_1 e^{-q_1T} - S_2 e^{-q_2T}$) |
| σ₁ = σ₂ = 0, in the money | gammas NaN | gammas 0 |

**Tests:** added `testEuroExchangeDeterministicRatio` to `MargrabeOptionTests`, covering both cases above plus an out-of-the-money zero-volatility case. It fails on master and passes with this change; the existing Margrabe and basket option tests still pass.

`AnalyticAmericanMargrabeEngine` computes the same combined variance; I'm happy to apply the clamp there too, here or in a separate PR.

review_comments.body: I would compare the variance with QL_EPSILON, instead of the stddev.
Done 👍, both checks now compare the variance with QL_EPSILON.

title: Handle deterministic asset ratio in the European Margrabe engine
